task: Track A — validate master→satellite MAC-derived auth credential claim from report 33

evidence.note: snprintf(local_120,0x101,"%s%s%s%s%s","NETGEAR_Orbi_",g_soapc_mac1,"_",g_soapc_mac2,"_password") then FUN_00029ce4 (MD5-hex-lowercase). Result copied to param_3 and also written to NVRAM soap_Authenticate_old_password. ALSO logged plaintext to /tmp/soapc_log.
MD5Init / MD5Update / MD5Final (OpenSSL libcrypto), then snprintf(__s,0x21,"%02x" x 16, ...) → lowercase hex, 32 chars + null.

evidence.topic: Master-side mac1 provenance (NOT a satellite field)
evidence.note: Reads NVRAM lan_ifname; get_eth_mac() on that interface → master's OWN LAN MAC; ether_etoa → "XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX"; sscanf splits 6 bytes; snprintf(local_7c,0x20,"%02X_%02X_%02X",byte3,byte4,byte5) → stored into g_soapc_mac1. The lower 3 bytes of the MASTER'S own LAN MAC.
evidence.correction: Corrects report 33 which left g_soapc_mac1 provenance ambiguous; it is NOT a satellite field.

evidence.note: snprintf key name "soapc_sat_%d_mac" with eventIndex, acosNvramConfig_get, sscanf, snprintf "%02X_%02X_%02X" of lower 3 bytes → g_soapc_mac2.

Concat of "NETGEAR_Orbi_" + <master-lower3-formatted-with-underscores> + "_" + <sat-lower3-formatted-with-underscores> + "_password". Final shape: NETGEAR_Orbi_XX_XX_XX_YY_YY_YY_password where XX*3 are master and YY*3 are sat. SIX hex pairs total but drawn from TWO devices, not one.
evidence.correction: Corrects report 35's wire-credential description ("MAC-derived"): it is a MIXED-MAC template, half master and half sat, not a single MAC.

evidence.note: Hardcoded literal "orbi" in SOAP envelope at 0x5d433 (uses getAuthPassword) and 0x5d242 (uses getNewAuthPassword). TWO authenticate templates exist in soapc.
evidence.new_finding: Second template getNewAuthPassword exists at 0x2c8b2/0x2d8b3 — purpose not fully traced in this pass but likely fires during an admin-password-rotation sync.

evidence.topic: Satellite-side validation — dynamic derivation (NOT NVRAM compare)
evidence.note: Sat does NOT compare incoming password to NVRAM http.password/http.passwordHash (as report 31 claimed). It (1) gets router.mac from nvram, (2) gets boarddata.mac0 from nvram (sat's own MAC), (3) converts both string→byte arrays, (4) snprintf's the template using bytes 3,4,5 of each (OUI-less lower half), (5) MD5s the result, (6) hex-encodes lowercase, (7) memcmp against the incoming password field.
evidence.correction: Material correction to report 31's claim that http.password/http.passwordHash is the compare target for satellite management auth. Those NVRAM keys exist but are used for a different auth context (likely admin web UI session, not this RPC-server entrypoint).

evidence.topic: Satellite-side router.mac auto-update via unauthenticated hyt pipeline
evidence.note: Inside the auth handler, BEFORE deriving the expected password, the sat runs: popen("(echo \"td s\"; usleep 500000) | hyt | grep \"Network relaying device\" | awk ... | cut -d ',' -f 1", "r"). If the fgets'd MAC differs from stored NVRAM router.mac, the sat does nvram_set("router.mac=%s") and nvram_commit(). hyt is the mesh daemon query; its response is not authenticated at this call site. An on-mesh attacker who can inject into the hyt dataset could cause the sat to rebase its expected-password router-side half.
evidence.severity_note: This is NOT a direct auth bypass — the attacker would still need to know (or discover) the sat's boarddata.mac0 lower-3 bytes. But it collapses the master-side mystery to zero: an on-mesh attacker who can speak to hyt effectively sets the master-half of the template they will later present.

evidence.topic: Satellite-side alternate auth: backhaul-passphrase direct compare
evidence.note: BEFORE the MD5 path, the sat reads NVRAM BhSta2.ssid+BhSta2.passphrase (falls back to BhSta5.*). If BhSta?.passphrase strlen==0x40 and all isxdigit, the sat snprintfs it into a buffer and compares (FUN_0001f8b8) against the incoming password. If they match, auth succeeds without going through the MD5 path. The backhaul passphrase is therefore a SECOND valid credential for this entrypoint.
evidence.severity_note: Not previously documented. Any party that learns the 802.11 backhaul passphrase (which is passed to the sat in-band during pairing and stored in NVRAM) can authenticate as the master.

evidence.note: (1) Username check memcmp-via-FUN_0001f7f8 replaced with strncasecmp → case-insensitive. (2) Success path now writes NVRAM legacy_auth_done=yes and commits; a prior `legacy_auth_done` sets a returned state code of 2 vs 0. (3) MD5 derivation logic itself is unchanged. These are relevant to CVE-0415's auth-relaxation surface but are not themselves a credential-derivation finding.
evidence.cve_relevance: Possible CVE-0415-adjacent (strncasecmp was a RELAXATION per report 34, not a tightening). Not conclusive.

evidence.note: In soapc, every SOAP envelope template references either getAuthPassword or getNewAuthPassword. Both resolve into FUN_0001f228 (NETGEAR_Orbi_ template) — the only in-code auth-password producer. There is no code path in soapc that uses a stored admin-password hash from NVRAM. Therefore the MAC-derived credential is the credential for EVERY master→sat management call in steady state, not just pre-pairing or provisioning.
evidence.correction: Upgrades report 31's "factory-default/pre-pairing fallback" framing to "primary steady-state credential", matching report 33's claim and extending it.

evidence.topic: Master-side TLS verification (sanity check of report 33's second PSIRT finding)
evidence.note: Not re-verified in this pass — orthogonal to Track A's credential-flow scope. Validation deferred to Track B.

FUN_0001f228 writes the computed MD5 hex string to this NVRAM key on every call via acosNvramConfig_set. This means a live master's NVRAM carries the current MAC-derived credential for the most-recently-addressed satellite. Readable via normal NVRAM introspection (Seal / nvram show on owner-rooted master).
evidence.severity_note: Credential-material-at-rest finding. Not a bypass by itself but reduces attacker work if they ever gain master read-access.

one_line_verdict: The master DOES send a MAC-derived credential in every satellite-management SOAP call, AND the satellite independently derives the same credential at validation time. The derivation is MD5-hex-lowercase("NETGEAR_Orbi_" + master-lower-3-bytes + "_" + sat-lower-3-bytes + "_password"), username literal "orbi". Materially corrects report 31's http.password compare-target claim and report 33's g_soapc_mac1 provenance.
material_corrections_to_prior_reports: Report 31 §3: sat auth validates against NVRAM http.password/http.passwordHash — WRONG for authenticate_satellite_1_svc. That function dynamically derives the expected MD5 at every call from NVRAM router.mac + boarddata.mac0. http.password/http.passwordHash are used by a different code path (admin web UI session via M1:Authenticate → soap_agent, not the authenticate_satellite_1_svc RPC server).
Report 33: g_soapc_mac1 provenance not stated — in fact it is the master's OWN LAN MAC lower-3-bytes, not a sat field. The composed credential is a MIXED-MAC template, not a sat-MAC template.
Report 31 §3 default-admin-password-derivation PSIRT: framed as a factory-fresh / pre-pairing fallback. In fact it is the PRIMARY steady-state credential for every master→sat management call.
new_psirt_findings_surfaced: Sat reads router MAC via unauthenticated popen of a hyt pipeline and auto-updates its NVRAM router.mac from it — potential mesh-level poisoning vector.
Backhaul passphrase (BhSta2.passphrase / BhSta5.passphrase, 64-hex-char Z→Z format) is a SECOND valid credential for authenticate_satellite_1_svc.
Computed credential is written to NVRAM soap_Authenticate_old_password on every call (credential-at-rest).
Computed credential is written plaintext to /tmp/soapc_log (credential in debug log).
